title: Matrix verification algorithm specification
statement: For every natural number $n$, Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and three $n\times n$ matrices over the two-element field, the verification program's output-and-cost law is the pushforward of a uniform Boolean string of length $n$ to the acceptance result and the stated cost. Its decision accepts on input $x$ exactly when $(C'-AB)x=0$, and it uses $n$ random bits. Its local work is at most $11(n+1)^2$ and is asymptotically bounded by a constant multiple of $(n+1)^2$. If $C'=AB$, uniform-input acceptance probability is one; if $C'\ne AB$, it is at most $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
